1.0.2.headline: A more capable canvas
1.0.2.summary: New navigation, grouping, and alignment tools make arranging references faster.

new.title: Hand tool and reworked toolbar
new.description: Move around the canvas with a dedicated Hand tool and open creation tools from the new Add drawer.

new.title: Visible group names
new.description: Group labels now appear above grouped items so boards stay easier to understand.

new.title: In-app release highlights
new.description: See what changed in RefBoard directly from the landing page after an update.

improved.title: Faster selection alignment
improved.description: Align and normalize tools now use clearer icons in the selection bar.

1.0.3.headline: Safer sessions, smoother boards
1.0.3.summary: RefBoard restores work more reliably while using less memory on large boards.

improved.title: Automatic session restore
improved.description: Your board returns automatically when RefBoard reopens.

improved.title: Faster canvas navigation
improved.description: Zooming and panning stay responsive on boards with many images.

improved.title: Lower memory usage
improved.description: Large boards now consume significantly less memory.

fixed.title: Images stay on the correct board
fixed.description: References from one board no longer occasionally appear in another.

fixed.title: Corrupted files open safely
fixed.description: Opening a damaged board no longer wipes the board already open.

1.0.4.headline: Sharper exports
1.0.4.summary: Copied and exported images now preserve their intended quality.

fixed.title: Crisp copied and exported images
fixed.description: Images no longer come out blurry after copying or exporting.

1.0.5.headline: Notes that feel natural
1.0.5.summary: Editing notes is more direct, with cleaner links, lists, and cursor behavior.

improved.title: Readable links while editing
improved.description: Notes show clickable link text instead of raw Markdown.

improved.title: Direct cursor placement
improved.description: Click anywhere in a note to place the cursor exactly there.

improved.title: Cleaner pasted content
improved.description: Checkboxes render properly, and pasted content keeps bullets from ChatGPT and the web.

fixed.title: Consistent note layout
fixed.description: Text alignment, spacing, and sizing issues in notes are resolved.

1.0.6.headline: A refreshed RefBoard
1.0.6.summary: A new identity and File Explorer previews make RefBoard feel at home on Windows.

new.title: New app icon
new.description: RefBoard has a refreshed visual identity across the app.

new.title: File Explorer previews
new.description: Saved RefBoard files now display a board thumbnail in File Explorer.

1.1.0.headline: A stronger everyday workflow
1.1.0.summary: This release brings better previews, cleaner notes, smarter pasting, and lower memory use.

new.title: File Explorer board thumbnails
new.description: Identify saved RefBoard files from their preview before opening them.

improved.title: More natural note editing
improved.description: Place the cursor with a click, use cleaner lists and checkboxes, and read links as clickable text.

improved.title: Smarter copy and paste
improved.description: Groups remain intact and pasted images arrive as individual references.

improved.title: Lower large-board memory use
improved.description: Image-heavy boards now use less system memory.

fixed.title: Smoother everyday navigation
fixed.description: Resolved the save prompt after export, landing-page wheel scrolling, and several zoom glitches.

1.1.1.headline: Faster, safer saves
1.1.1.summary: Large boards now save, reopen, and switch more reliably with lower peak memory use.

improved.title: Atomic board saves
improved.description: Boards write to a temporary file first, so a failed save cannot damage the existing file.

improved.title: Much faster large-board saves
improved.description: A 22 MB board can now save in well under a second.

improved.title: Lower copy memory use
improved.description: Copying large selections requires far less memory.

improved.title: Instant reopen for the active board
improved.description: Opening the board already in use no longer reloads or decodes its images.

improved.title: Earlier memory release
improved.description: Switching boards frees old image data sooner and lowers peak usage.

fixed.title: Reliable close and Home actions
fixed.description: Timed-out saves keep the board open instead of leaving RefBoard hanging.

fixed.title: Clean File Explorer thumbnails
fixed.description: The duplicate R logo is gone; the preview badge appears once in the bottom-right corner.

1.1.2.headline: More control from canvas to export
1.1.2.summary: High-resolution crops, drawing shortcuts, batch naming, and disk-backed loading expand the creative workflow.

new.title: Full-resolution cropped exports
new.description: Export only the visible crop while preserving the source image resolution.

new.title: Drawing keyboard shortcuts
new.description: Press E for the eraser, or use [ and ] to change pen thickness.

new.title: Normalize by width or height
new.description: Match selected images by a shared dimension instead of scale alone.

new.title: Flexible batch export names
new.description: Number exports in order with padded digits or keep original file names.

improved.title: Exact crop dimensions
improved.description: The export dialog shows the precise pixel size of the cropped result.

improved.title: Disk-backed image streaming
improved.description: Large boards load faster and use less memory.

fixed.title: Cleaner landing-page thumbnails
fixed.description: Stray black blocks no longer appear in board previews.

fixed.title: Stable notes and groups at extreme zoom
fixed.description: Note cursor behavior and group rendering remain reliable far in or out.

1.1.3.headline: Sharper at every zoom
1.1.3.summary: This update focuses on image stability and smoother rendering.

fixed.title: Consistent image sharpness
fixed.description: Images remain crisp while zooming in and out.

fixed.title: Seamless quality switching
fixed.description: References change rendering quality without visibly popping.

2.0.0.headline: Introducing Animatics
2.0.0.summary: RefBoard 2.0 turns your reference boards into motion, with a redesigned interface and a whole new way to work.

new.title: Animatics timeline
new.description: Turn references into motion with a layered timeline, audio tracks, and precise in/out controls.

new.title: Export to Premiere & After Effects
new.description: Hand off your animatic straight to your editing and compositing workflow.

new.title: Themes
new.description: Personalize RefBoard's look with a refreshed, themeable interface.

improved.title: Redesigned interface
improved.description: A cleaner, more focused workspace across the board and landing screens.

improved.title: Board Save As
improved.description: Save a copy of any board without overwriting your original.

2.0.1.headline: Faster saves, smoother animatics, and export fixes
2.0.1.summary: This update fixes Premiere Pro export, speeds up saving large boards, and adds timeline polish.

improved.title: Faster board saving
improved.description: Large boards now save noticeably faster.

improved.title: Save indicator
improved.description: A subtle indicator confirms when your board has been saved.

improved.title: Snap timeline markers
improved.description: In and out points now snap to clip edges when snapping is on.

fixed.title: Premiere Pro export
fixed.description: Fixed exported timelines failing to import into Premiere Pro.

fixed.title: Window dragging in animatics
fixed.description: The app window can now be moved while in the animatics editor.

2.0.2.headline: Cleaner starts, faster boards
2.0.2.summary: RefBoard opens large boards faster, starts fresh on launch, and restores your file previews.

new.title: Choose when to restore
new.description: RefBoard now opens to your home screen. If you left unsaved work, a card offers to restore it — so you start fresh unless you choose otherwise.

improved.title: Faster board opening
improved.description: Large boards open roughly twice as fast, showing your images sooner.

fixed.title: Board previews restored
fixed.description: Saved boards again show their image preview as the file thumbnail in Explorer.

fixed.title: Saving after restore
fixed.description: A restored board now saves back to its original file instead of prompting for a new one.

2.0.3.headline: Multiple boards, smoother canvas
2.0.3.summary: Open up to four RefBoard windows at once, paste images between them correctly, and work large boards without the blur flicker.

new.title: Work on multiple boards at once
new.description: Open up to four RefBoard windows from the home screen so you can compare and edit separate boards side by side.

improved.title: Smoother large boards
improved.description: Zooming and panning stay steadier on boards with hundreds of images, with faster quality catch-up when you stop navigating.

improved.title: True cross-window paste
improved.description: Copying images from one board window into another now pastes each image's real pixels, not a flattened blank placeholder.

fixed.title: Zoom blur flicker removed
fixed.description: Images no longer flash blurry on and off while zooming as resolution tiers change.

fixed.title: Saving with two windows open
fixed.description: Saving one board while another window is open no longer fails after pasting images between them.

2.0.4.headline: Reliable drawing, stable zoom
2.0.4.summary: Draw and erase confidently on copied images, undo instantly, and keep every stroke visible while zooming even on image-heavy boards.

new.title: Direct drawing shortcuts
new.description: Press D to activate the pen or E to activate the eraser, even when drawing mode is not already open.

improved.title: Smoother image-heavy boards
improved.description: Zooming through boards with 100 or more images stays sharp and stable without severe blur jumps.

fixed.title: Independent drawing on copied images
fixed.description: Painting or erasing a duplicated or pasted image no longer changes the original image or its other copies.

fixed.title: Reliable drawing undo and redo
fixed.description: Ctrl+Z and redo now update the visible painted pixels immediately instead of leaving a stale stroke on the board.

fixed.title: Paint stays visible while zooming
fixed.description: New strokes no longer disappear or flicker when the image switches between proxy, detail, and full-resolution rendering.

fixed.title: Safe interrupted strokes
fixed.description: Pointer cancellation, window focus changes, and drawing-mode exit now finalize strokes without leaving drawing stuck.

2.0.5.headline: Steadier image quality on big boards
2.0.5.summary: Boards with hundreds of images hold their sharpness better while you zoom, and images scrolling into view load detail right away instead of waiting for you to stop.

improved.title: Sharp images stay sharp
improved.description: An image whose full detail is already loaded now always draws at that detail. Previously it could fall back to a low-resolution preview when the board was busy, even though the sharp version was ready to use.

improved.title: Steadier quality while zooming
improved.description: The renderer now keeps its quality decisions from one frame to the next, so images no longer swap back and forth between detail levels as the view moves under the cursor.

fixed.title: Images entering view during zoom
fixed.description: An image scrolling into view while you zoom now loads its real detail immediately instead of staying on a low-resolution preview until the zoom stops.

2.0.6.headline: Pin, fill, and a safer board
2.0.6.summary: Keep RefBoard above other windows, erase objects from images with a lasso fill, and recover the last good board after a crash.

new.title: Always on top
new.description: A pin in the title bar keeps RefBoard above other windows, or attached above a window you pick.

new.title: Content-aware fill
new.description: Press C or use the wand next to Draw, lasso something on an image, and release to erase and fill from nearby pixels. Undo restores the original. Shared copies stay untouched.

improved.title: Softer fill edges
improved.description: The fill blends a few pixels at the lasso rim instead of leaving a hard cut.

improved.title: Black and Tide themes
improved.description: Two new appearance themes in settings.

improved.title: Clearer rotate cursor
improved.description: Corner rotate uses a 32px PureRef-style cursor.

fixed.title: Wheel over the pin list
fixed.description: Scrolling the "always on top of" window list no longer zooms the board.

fixed.title: Last good board after a crash
fixed.description: RefBoard keeps a last-good copy so a crash is less likely to lose the board you were working on.

2.0.7.headline: Lighter, faster, easier to find things in
2.0.7.summary: RefBoard is a moodboard app again: animatics and content-aware fill are gone, images snap to each other properly, and Home gets search and renaming.

new.title: Search your boards from Home
new.description: Filter Recent Works by board name or the folder it lives in. Ctrl+F jumps to the field, and matches are highlighted on the cards.

new.title: Rename a board without leaving RefBoard
new.description: The pencil on a Home card (or F2) renames the board in place. It renames the real .refboard file on disk, keeps its backup and thumbnail, and refuses names the file system would reject.

new.title: Search a board from the toolbar
new.description: A search button sits in the left toolbar, so finding notes and images on a board no longer depends on knowing Ctrl+F.

improved.title: Images snap to each other, not to a grid
improved.description: Edge magnetism is rebuilt PureRef-style and is on by default: images butt together with no gap, edges line up down a column, and a snap holds until you clearly pull away. The dot grid is decoration only now, so it no longer quantizes every drag to 10px.

improved.title: A lighter install
improved.description: Dropping animatics and content-aware fill takes the installer from 115 MB to 86 MB, and RefBoard no longer loads a video toolchain at startup whether or not you ever used one.

improved.title: A quieter Home
improved.description: The landing page is reworked into a calmer recents workspace.

improved.title: Autosave admits when it fails
improved.description: A failed session autosave used to report success anyway. It now raises a warning that offers Save board... and names the cause, including running out of storage quota.

improved.title: Leaner undo on big boards
improved.description: Undo history is capped by memory as well as by step count, so a long session on a large board no longer holds hundreds of megabytes of snapshots.

fixed.title: Animatics removed
fixed.description: The timeline, audio, time remap and Premiere/After Effects export are gone — a second app had grown inside a moodboard app. Boards saved by 2.0.6 still open, but any audio and video they held is skipped.

fixed.title: Content-aware fill removed
fixed.description: The lasso fill tool is no longer in the toolbar. It was too heavy and unreliable for everyday moodboard work.

fixed.title: Groups keep their contents
fixed.description: Arrow-keying a selected group moved the frame and left the images behind, and resizing one dropped them too. Both now move what they contain, and a nudge can be undone.

fixed.title: Group selection frame rotates with the images
fixed.description: The multi-select box stayed axis-aligned during a rotate, so it swelled and shrank under itself and the corner handles slid away from the pointer.

fixed.title: Copied images keep their original bytes
fixed.description: Copying an image to the clipboard re-encoded it. It now hands over the original file data.

2.0.8.headline: Large boards stay sharp
2.0.8.summary: On a board of a few hundred images, some images used to render visibly blurry while their neighbours stayed crisp — and which ones shifted as you moved around. Decoded image memory is now sized to your machine instead of to a fixed 31 MB, and adjustable. Image export, which 2.0.7 broke outright, works again.

new.title: Decoded image memory setting
new.description: Settings → Performance gains a Decoded image memory control. Auto sizes it from your machine's RAM — 512 MB on 8 GB and up, 256 MB on smaller machines — and you can pin it to 256 MB, 512 MB, 1 GB or 2 GB instead. Raising it lets more images stay sharp at the same time on a large board. RefBoard only uses what the current view actually needs, so the number is a ceiling rather than a reservation.

improved.title: Sharpening follows what you are looking at
improved.description: Pending image work is now started in order of how close each image sits to the middle of your view, and the queue holds eight times as much. Before, work ran strictly in the order it was requested, and an overfull queue threw away the oldest request — which was usually the image right in front of you.

improved.title: A missed budget costs sharpness, not legibility
improved.description: An image that cannot be decoded at the resolution your current zoom wants now falls back to a 512px surface rather than the 256px preview, so it reads as slightly soft instead of plainly blurry. RefBoard also stops reclaiming a surface the instant it loses its place for a single frame, so panning back over an image no longer re-decodes it from nothing.

fixed.title: Images stop going blurry on boards of 200 or more
fixed.description: Decoded images were rationed by two fixed 31 MB budgets. Because an image smaller than the resolution it needs is decoded whole, an ordinary board of 600–900px references pushed nearly every visible image into one of those budgets, about a dozen fit, and everything else was drawn from a 256px preview. On a 240-image test board with 32 images on screen, 14 were being drawn from the preview at less than half the resolution they needed; now none are, and none are during a pan either.

fixed.title: One oversized image no longer softens the whole screen
fixed.description: An image larger than the entire decode budget was accepted anyway whenever it happened to be nearest the pointer, which spent the whole budget on that one image and dropped every other image on screen to its preview in the same frame. It now waits until the budget would otherwise go unused, so it still sharpens on its own but never at the cost of its neighbours.

fixed.title: The image under the cursor stops hogging priority
fixed.description: Scroll-zooming over an image gave it absolute priority for five seconds afterwards, holding the images around it on their previews long after you had moved on. That window is now 1.2 seconds — long enough to outlast the gesture, short enough that where the pointer came to rest stops mattering.

fixed.title: Choosing an export folder works again
fixed.description: In 2.0.7 the Browse button in Export images did nothing at all. The main process had stopped answering the folder-picker request, so the click failed silently — and because the folder field is read-only, Browse was the only way to fill it. Exporting images was effectively unusable in the desktop app. The picker opens again, parented to the window you started it from, and a picker that cannot open now says so instead of failing quietly.

fixed.title: One export, not one save dialog per image
fixed.description: With no folder set, Export fell back to saving each image as a separate browser download, which opened its own Save As dialog for every image — exporting twenty references meant dismissing twenty dialogs. RefBoard now writes the whole batch to the chosen folder in one step, and if the folder is empty it asks you to pick one instead of starting anything.

fixed.title: Export starts in a real folder by default
fixed.description: The export folder no longer opens blank on a machine that has never exported. It defaults to Documents\RefBoard Exports again, and still remembers the last folder you chose.

2.0.9.headline: Drag images out, and a copy that keeps up
2.0.9.summary: Images can now leave RefBoard by being dragged straight into another application. Copying is around eleven times faster than it was, and a cropped export no longer quietly costs you a generation of JPEG quality.

new.title: Drag images out into another app
new.description: A grip in the selection bar drags the selected images out as real files — into Photoshop, Explorer, a browser upload field, anywhere that accepts a drop. An image you have not cropped or altered hands over its original file untouched; a cropped, rotated or painted one is written out to match what the board shows. Several selected images become several files, and two references that share a filename arrive as two files instead of one overwriting the other.

improved.title: Copying is about eleven times faster
improved.description: Copying one 4000×3000 photo took 1.45 seconds, and twenty-four references took 1.33; both now take roughly a tenth of a second. Nearly all of that time went on rendering and PNG-encoding the whole selection at up to 8192 pixels before copy would say anything at all. The flattened image placed on the clipboard is now capped at 1024 pixels. Pasting back into RefBoard is unaffected — it rebuilds the real images at their full size — and dragging an image out still hands over the untouched original.

improved.title: A cropped export keeps every pixel
improved.description: Cropping forces an image to be encoded again, and a cropped JPEG used to be written back out as a JPEG, quietly costing a second generation of compression on pixels you asked to keep. It now comes out as a PNG, so the result is identical to the crop. A cropped WebP stays WebP, encoded losslessly, which is both exact and smaller than the same image as a PNG. Choosing JPEG or WebP yourself in the export dialog still gives you that format. The dialog now says when a JPEG is about to become a PNG, and the filename preview shows the extension you will actually get.

fixed.title: Copying a JPEG never kept its original bytes
fixed.description: Copy tried to hand the clipboard the untouched JPEG file, which the clipboard has never accepted — PNG is the only image type it takes. Every JPEG copy therefore attempted a write that could not succeed, and then rendered the full-size PNG it had been trying to avoid, which is where most of the delay came from. Copy now goes straight to the render, and keeping the original bytes applies where it genuinely works: a single untouched PNG.

fixed.title: Copy stopped encoding an image it then threw away
fixed.description: To keep its clipboard payload small, copy downscaled every large image to 2048 pixels, re-encoded it as a PNG, and kept that only if it came out smaller than the original. For a photograph it never does. On a 4000×3000 JPEG this was 336 milliseconds spent producing a 5.9 MB PNG that was discarded in favour of the 3.9 MB original. It is now only attempted for the source formats that can actually come out smaller.

fixed.title: Help stopped claiming it was version 1.0.1
fixed.description: The footer of the keyboard-shortcuts window had the version written into it by hand and was never updated, so it has read "RefBoard v1.0.1" through eight releases while Settings showed the real one. It now reads the running version, like Settings does.
